highlights:
A Monthly Active User (MAU) is defined as a registered and logged-in Snapchat user who visits Snapchat through our applications or websites at least once during the 30-day period ending on the calendar month-end. We calculate average Monthly Active Users for a particular quarter by calculating the average of the MAUs as of each calendar month-end in that quarter.

Beginning with our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q to be filed for the first quarter of 2027, we plan to transition to global MAU as our primary audience metric. This change will include the replacement of global DAU with global MAU, as well as the discontinuation of regional DAU and regional ARPU. While DAU remains an important measure of engagement, we no longer believe it is the best primary measure of long-term value. MAU represents the scale of our community, while engagement and monetization metrics reflect the depth and value of our service. Daily engagement has historically been stable as a percentage of monthly engagement, but we do not intend to optimize Snapchat around daily use at the expense of long-term value for our community. A longer-term horizon better aligns our reported metrics with the product and safety decisions that strengthen relationships, create lasting utility, and support broader, more durable audience growth. Alongside global MAU, we are introducing global MAU-based ARPU as our primary monetization metric. The following describes these user metrics both prior to and after our planned transition.

...

We define a Monthly Active User, or MAU, as a registered and logged-in Snapchat user who visits Snapchat through our applications or websites at least once during the 30-day period ending on the calendar month-end. We calculate average MAUs for a particular quarter by calculating the average of the MAUs as of each calendar month-end in that quarter. Beginning in the first quarter of 2027, we plan to update the definition of MAU to include any registered and logged-in Snapchat user who visits at least one Snapchat-branded product through our applications or websites, which under the updated definition will include users who access our products through Apple Watch. Historically, MAU attributable to Apple Watch users has not been material. Additionally, beginning in the first quarter of 2027, MAU will be calculated using activity during the last 30 days of the quarter. Accordingly, reported quarterly MAU will represent the number of active users as of quarter end rather than an average of monthly active users during the quarter. We believe this measurement period provides a more current view of our trajectory and improves comparability with peers. The impact of these changes to our historical MAU definition would have resulted in a less than 1% change to our historical MAU in the third quarter of 2026 and would have resulted in similarly immaterial changes in our historical MAUs in each quarter from the first quarter of 2024 to the second quarter of 2026.

Changes in our ... Technical issues may result in data not being recorded from every user’s application. For example, because some Snapchat features can be used without internet connectivity, we may not count a DAU or MAU because we don’t receive timely notice that a user has opened the Snapchat application. This undercounting may increase as we grow in Rest of World markets where users may have poor connectivity. We do not adjust our reported metrics to reflect this underreporting. We believe that we have adequate controls to collect user metrics; however, there is no uniform industry standard. We continually seek to identify these technical issues and improve both our accuracy and precision, including ensuring that our investors and others can understand the factors impacting our business, but these technical issues and new issues may continue in the future, including if there continues to be no uniform industry standard.

We have multiple pipelines of user data that we use to determine whether a user has visited Snapchat through our applications or websites during the applicable measurement period. This provides redundancy in the event one pipeline of data were to become unavailable for technical reasons, and also gives us redundant data to help measure how users interact with our applications and websites.

results.title: Snap Inc. (via Public) / Quarterly Report for Quarter Ending September 30, 2026 (Form 10-Q)
highlights:
Overview of Third Quarter 2026 Results 

 Our key user metrics and financial results for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were as follows: 

 User Metrics 

 • Monthly Active Users, or MAUs, increased 4% year-over-year to 977 million. 

 • Daily Active Users, or DAUs, increased 4% year-over-year to 495 million. 

 • Average revenue per user, or ARPU, was $3.48, compared to $3.16 in the prior year.

...

Trends in User Metrics 

 We define MAU as a registered and logged-in Snapchat user who visits Snapchat through our applications or websites at least once during the 30-day period ending on the calendar month-end. We calculate average MAUs for a particular quarter by calculating the average of the MAUs as of each calendar month-end in that quarter. We define a DAU as a registered and logged-in Snapchat user who visits Snapchat through our applications or websites at least once during a defined 24-hour period. We calculate average DAUs for a particular quarter by adding the number of DAUs on each day of that quarter and dividing that sum by the number of days in that quarter. DAUs are broken out by geography because markets have different characteristics. We define ARPU as quarterly revenue divided by the average DAUs.

...

In the first quarter of 2027, among other changes to our user metrics, we plan to transition to global MAU as our primary audience metric. For a description of these changes, see the "Note Regarding User Metrics and Other Data" included elsewhere in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q. 

 User Engagement 

 We had 977 million MAUs on average in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 34 million, or 4%, from the third quarter of 2025.

results.author: Motley Fool Transcribing
highlights:
- Revenue: $1.72 billion, representing 14% growth year over year.
- Net Income: $56 million, reflecting an improvement of $160 million from a net loss in the previous year.
- Adjusted EBITDA: $383 million, growing 110% year over year with a margin of 22%.
- Gross Margin: 62%, expanding by approximately 7 percentage points due to revenue growth and cost efficiencies.
- Daily Active Users: 495 million, an increase of 4% year over year.
- Monthly Active Users: 977 million, representing 4% growth year over year.
- Operating Cash Flow: $210 million, an increase of 44% year over year.
- Free Cash Flow: $164 million, rising 76% year over year.
- Other Revenue: Grew 84% year over year, driven by subscriptions to Snapchat+, Memories Storage, and Lens+.
- Paid Subscribers: Surpassed 30 million across the company's premium offerings.
- Advertising Revenue: Grew 4% year over year, with direct response advertising offset by declines in brand advertising.
- Spotlight Engagement: Daily active viewers increased 40% year over year, while the number of people posting to the platform grew 130%.
- Direct Response Revenue: Reached 77% of total revenue, representing a significant increase from the previous year.
- App Purchase Revenue: Increased over 54% year over year as purchase volume for optimized campaigns more than doubled.
- Web Purchase Revenue: Grew 11% year over year, supported by a 31% increase in total purchases.
- Sponsored Snaps: Revenue grew 56% sequentially as chat's share of total revenue rose 8 percentage points year over year.
- Promoted Places: Revenue and advertiser adoption both more than doubled on a sequential basis.
- Operating Leverage: Approximately 93% of incremental revenue flowed through to adjusted EBITDA.
- Infrastructure Costs Guidance: Anticipated at $1.65 billion to $1.66 billion for the full year.
- Q4 Revenue Guidance: Targeted between $1.950 billion and $1.985 billion.
- Q4 Adjusted EBITDA Guidance: Range of $490 million to $525 million.

results.title: Snap tumbles on revenue, user growth miss; announces metric shift By Investing.com
results.author: Luke Juricic
highlights:
Daily active users (DAUs) rose 3.8% from a year earlier to 495 million, below the 499.31 million analysts expected.

North America fell 6.1% to 92 million users, slightly above the 91.92 million estimate. Europe was flat at 98 million, just under the 98.29 million estimate. Rest of world rose 8.9% to 305 million, missing the 309.08 million estimate and accounting for most of the growth.

Snap announced it will shift its primary audience metric from daily active users to monthly active users (MAUs) starting in the first quarter of 2027. The company said it will pursue a "longer-term horizon" that better aligns with product decisions, though it acknowledged this approach means not optimizing "around daily use at the expense of long-term value."
